mainTopic: When a husband and wife die together in a collapsed house and no one knows who died first, who inherits her property and her כתובה?
overview: This amud is a new משנה. A house falls on a husband and wife, and nobody knows which of them died first. The order matters. If the wife died first, her husband inherited her before he died, so his heirs take everything. If the husband died first, her own family gets her property and her כתובה. בית שמאי say that since the facts can't be known, the two sides split the disputed property. בית הלל disagree and leave each kind of property with whoever already held it. The property she brought in under guarantee stays in its prior status. The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs. The property that comes into and goes out of the marriage with her stays with her father's heirs.

steps.title: The case: a house falls on husband and wife
steps.stepSummary: The משנה sets up a case of doubt. A husband and wife die together, and each side's heirs claim that the other spouse died first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a house fell on a man and his wife, the husband's heirs say the wife died first and then the husband. The wife's heirs say the husband died first and then the wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays out the case and the two opposite claims. It is setting up the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Who died first decides who inherits. If the wife died first, her husband inherited her before he died, so his heirs take her property too. If the husband died first, she never passed anything to him, so her own family gets her property and her כתובה.
steps.confusionAlert: Each side is not arguing about who is a 'better' heir. Everything depends on the order of death, because a husband inherits his wife only if he was still alive when she died.

phrases.english: If the house fell on him and on his wife,

phrases.notes: So the husband inherited her first, and his heirs now take it all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה about doubtful order of death between husband and wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A case of doubt is presented. Each side's heirs claim the order of death that favors them.

steps.title: בית שמאי: the two sides split it
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי rule that since we cannot know who died first, the two sets of heirs divide the disputed property.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: they divide it.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי give their ruling. Because the facts can never be known, the two sides split the property in question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both claims are equally possible and neither side has proof. So בית שמאי treat it as a true tie and give each side half.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt that cannot be settled

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first ruling on the case of doubt set up in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the order of death is unknown, the heirs split the disputed property.

steps.title: בית הלל: each kind of property stays where it was
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל do not split anything. Each type of property stays with whoever held it before. The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs. The property that comes into and goes out of the marriage with her stays with her father's heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say: the property stays in its place. The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs. The property that comes in and goes out with her stays with the father's heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give a different ruling. They split the property into types and leave each type with the side that already held it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of dividing in half, בית הלל sort the disputed property into three kinds and leave each with whoever already held it (חזקה). First, the property she brought into the marriage under guarantee (נְכָסִים) stays in its prior status. Second, the כתובה is paid from the husband's property, so it stays with his heirs. Third, the property that goes in and out of the marriage with her stays with her side, her father's heirs.

keyTerms.meaning: In their established status, staying with whoever held them
The marriage contract payment owed to the wife
Property that comes into the marriage and goes out with her (נִכְסֵי מְלוֹג)
The heirs of her father, meaning her family

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי split the doubtful property. בית הלל leave each kind where it stands: the כתובה with the husband's heirs, and the property that comes and goes with her with her father's heirs.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Father's heirs' here means the wife's own heirs, her relatives from her father's family. It does not mean the property goes back to her father personally. If the husband did not inherit her, her inheritance passes to them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic example of deciding a doubt by leaving things in their existing status rather than splitting them. The גמרא will build its discussion on it.

phrases.english: the property remains in its status,
phrases.notes: The משנה doesn't spell out here whose status this means; the גמרא will discuss it.

phrases.english: the marriage contract — in the possession of the husband's heirs,
property that comes in and goes out with her —
in the possession of the father's heirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with בית שמאי: instead of splitting, each kind of property stays in its existing status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Property stays in its prior status. The כתובה stays with the husband's heirs, and the property that comes and goes with her stays with her father's heirs.
